title: Patterning the Geometry of Human Embryonic Stem Cell Colonies on Compliant Substrates to Control Tissue-Level Mechanics
protocol: Create a photomask with desired geometric features.
Use computer-aided drafting software to design the features.
For use with negative photoresist, make features opaque and the remainder of the mask transparent.
Spin coat negative photoresist onto a 100 mm silicon wafer.
Determine the speed and length of spin to generate a film thickness of 100-250 µm using the photoresist data sheet.
Process the photoresist according to the product data sheet, typically involving a soft bake.
UV expose with photomask in a mask aligner.
Post exposure bake.
Develop the exposed photoresist.
Hard bake the developed wafer.
Place 18 mm diameter #1 thickness coverslips into a glass Petri dish.
Add 20 mL of 1 M HCl to the Petri dish and gently shake the dish to disperse the coverslips.
Ensure all the coverslips are submerged and release air bubbles from between the coverslips.
Incubate overnight at room temperature with gentle shaking.
Decant HCl from the dish.
Add 20 mL of ultrapure water and wash with gentle shaking for 10 min.
Discard water and repeat for a total of five washes.
After discarding the final wash, add 20 mL of 100% ethanol to the dish.
Using forceps, remove the coverslips individually and arrange between two pieces of filter paper to dry.
Store dried coverslips in a sealed container.
Place 18 mm diameter #1 thickness coverslips into a Petri dish.
Add 20 mL of 0.2 M HCl to the petri dish.
Gently shake the dish to disperse the coverslips.
Ensure all the coverslips are submerged and release air bubbles from between the coverslips.
Incubate overnight at room temperature with gentle shaking.
Decant HCl from the dish.
Add 20 mL of ultrapure water and wash with gentle shaking for 10 min.
Discard water and repeat for a total of five washes.
After discarding the final wash, add 20 mL of 0.1 M NaOH and shake gently to disperse and submerge coverslips.
Incubate at room temperature with gentle shaking for 1 h.
Decant NaOH from the dish.
Add 20 mL of ultrapure water and wash with gentle shaking for 10 min.
Discard water and repeat for a total of five washes.
After discarding the final wash, add 20 mL of a 1:200 dilution of 3-aminopropyltrimethoxysilane in ultrapure water and shake gently to disperse and submerge coverslips.
Incubate at room temperature with gentle shaking for 1 h or overnight.
Decant the diluted 3-aminopropyltrimethoxysilane solution from the dish.
Add 20 mL of ultrapure water and wash with gentle shaking for 10 min.
Discard water and repeat for a total of at least five washes.
After discarding the final wash, add 20 mL of a 1:140 dilution of 70% glutaraldehyde in phosphate buffered saline (PBS) and shake gently to disperse and submerge coverslips.
Incubate at room temperature with gentle shaking for 1 h or overnight.
Decant the diluted glutaraldehyde solution from the dish.
Add 20 mL of ultrapure water and wash with gentle shaking for 10 min.
Discard water and repeat for a total of five washes.
After discarding the final wash, add 20 mL of 100% ethanol.
Using forceps, remove the coverslips individually and arrange between two pieces of filter paper to dry.
Store dried coverslips in a sealed container.
Mix PDMS base with PDMS curing agent at a 10:1 ratio, by weight.
Mix thoroughly.
Degas the PDMS mixture in a desiccator for 30-60 min or until all air bubbles are removed.
Place the modified silicon wafer into a plastic 100 mm dish.
Slowly and evenly pour the PDMS mixture over the surface of the wafer.
Tap the dish on the work surface to release air bubbles from the wafer.
Degas the PDMS mixture for 10 minutes or until all air bubbles are removed.
Bake the PDMS at 70 °C for 2 hours.
Allow the PDMS to cool to room temperature.
Cut out the section of PDMS from the center of the dish containing geometric features.
Cut the PDMS into roughly 10 x 10 mm squares, each containing features for a single experimental condition.
Mix PDMS base with PDMS curing agent at an 8:1 ratio by weight.
Prepare approximately 20 g of PDMS mixture for each 100 mm dish.
Mix the PDMS thoroughly.
Degas the PDMS mixture in a desiccator for 30-60 minutes or until all air bubbles are removed.
Slowly and evenly pour the PDMS into a clean 100 mm dish.
Tap the dish on the work surface to release any air bubbles.
Bake the PDMS at 70 °C for 2 hours.
Allow the PDMS to cool to room temperature.
Remove the PDMS from the dish.
Invert the PDMS such that the surface that was in contact with the bottom of the dish is facing up.
Cut a 15 x 15 mm square of PDMS for each stamp generated.
Arrange flat slabs of PDMS on the lid of a 150 mm dish or other flat surface for easier handling.
Ensure sufficient spacing between slabs (e.g., arrange nine flat slabs with even spacing).
Invert each stamp generated in Step 3.1 onto a flat slab of PDMS such that features on the stamp are in contact with the PDMS.
Gently press on the top of the stamp with forceps to ensure even contact.
Prop the lid holding PDMS stamp/slab pairs up on the base of the dish at an angle.
Place a small drop of UV-curable polymer at the top interface of each stamp/slab pair.
The polymer will be wicked between the two by surface tension, assisted by gravity.
Place a small drop of UV-curable polymer at each of the remaining three sides of each stamp/slab interface.
Using a 200 µL pipette tip, connect the drops of polymer around the edges of the stamp/slab interface.
Carefully place the stamp/slab pairs into a UV-sterilization box.
Expose the stamp/slab pairs for 10 min using the sterile "Str" power setting.
Gently remove the PDMS stamp while holding down the flat slab and stencil that formed from the UV-curable polymer.
Carefully remove the stencil and invert it such that the surface that was in contact with the flat slab of PDMS is facing up.
Place the inverted stencils back into a UV-sterilization box.
Expose the inverted stencils for 3 min using the sterile "Str" power setting.
Place one acid-washed coverslip for each stencil onto a clean piece of laboratory film.
Carefully place each stencil, flat-side-down, onto an acid-washed coverslip.
Firmly and evenly press down on the stencil to create strong contact between the stencil and the coverslip.
Press firmly across the entire surface of the stencil to ensure sufficient contact.
Pipette 100 μL of ultrapure sterile water onto the surface of each stencil.
Incubate at room temperature for 1 hour to check for leaking.
Aspirate water from successfully bonded stencils and proceed with plasma cleaning.
Place the coverslips with stencils into a plasma cleaner.
Apply high power plasma for 30 seconds.
Prepare sterile 100 mM HEPES, 100 mM NaCl solution on ice.
Add matrigel to achieve a concentration of 225 μg/mL once ice cold.
Add collagen to achieve a concentration of 25 μg/mL.
Include a fluorescently tagged ligand in the ligand solution for troubleshooting or visualization.
Pipette the ligand solution onto the surface of each stencil.
Apply 100 µL per stencil for stencils made from 10 x 10 mm square stamps.
Check for air bubbles in stencil features.
Remove air bubbles from features if necessary using fine-tipped forceps or a 2 µL pipette tip.
Aspirate the ligand solution from the surface of a stencil.
Collect and store the ligand solution at 4 °C for reuse up to a month.
Briefly submerge the coverslip with stencil into a dish containing sterile PBS to wash.
Briefly submerge the coverslip with stencil into a second dish of sterile PBS to wash.
Remove the stencil from the surface of the coverslip carefully.
Submerge the coverslip into a dish containing ultrapure sterile water to remove salts.
Tap the edge of the coverslip to a delicate task wipe to wick away excess water.
Dry the coverslip under an inert gas, such as nitrogen.
Mark the underside of the coverslip to keep track of orientation from this point forward.
Sterilize all cap holders, tubes, and spacers used to make polyacrylamide gels by washing with 10% bleach overnight.
Rinse sterilized items with water at least five times to remove bleach.
Wash sterilized items briefly in 70% ethanol.
Place all pieces on delicate task wipes in a sterile biosafety cabinet to dry before use.
Prepare polyacrylamide solution to obtain desired hydrogel elasticity.
Mix together all components except the fluorescent microspheres and potassium persulfate (PPS).
Prepare 1% potassium persulfate solution fresh each time.
Degas the polyacrylamide solution under vacuum for 30 min.
Degas microspheres under vacuum for 30 min.
Degas PPS under vacuum for 30 min.
Briefly sonicate microspheres after degassing.
Add appropriate volume of microspheres to polyacrylamide solution by pipetting up and down, being careful not to introduce air bubbles.
Briefly sonicate the mixture.
Add appropriate volume of PPS to the polyacrylamide solution by pipetting up and down, being careful not to introduce air bubbles.
Pipette 75-150 µL to the center of each glutaraldehyde-activated coverslip.
Place a patterned coverslip onto each glutaraldehyde-activated coverslip with polyacrylamide and spacer, ensuring the patterned ligand faces the polyacrylamide solution.
Touch the side of each polyacrylamide "sandwich" to a delicate task wipe to wick away excess polyacrylamide solution.

Place each polyacrylamide "sandwich" into a cap holder with threads compatible with 15 mL conical-bottom tubes, ensuring the bottom of the glutaraldehyde coverslip is in contact with the bottom of the cap holder and the patterned coverslip is on top.
Screw a 15 mL conical-bottom tube into each cap holder to hold the polyacrylamide "sandwiches" in place without overtightening.
Centrifuge the polyacrylamide "sandwiches" in swing-buckets at 200 x g for 10 min at room temperature.
Place the tubes in tube racks after centrifugation to maintain orientation for an additional 50 min.
Cover the tubes with foil during polymerization to prevent bleaching of fluorescent microspheres.
Centrifuge the mixture as required for TFM.
Transfer the polyacrylamide "sandwich" from tubes and submerge in PBS in a 100 mm dish.
Wrap the submerged "sandwich" with laboratory film and incubate at room temperature or overnight at 4°C.
Carefully remove the patterned coverslip and spacer from the polyacrylamide "sandwich" while it remains submerged in PBS.
Place each coverslip with patterned polyacrylamide into a cap holder.
Place a gasket (18 mm outer diameter, 14 mm inner diameter) on top of the coverslip and around the polyacrylamide where the spacer was located.
Screw a sawed-off 15 mm conical-bottom tube into the cap holder to form a well with the patterned polyacrylamide at the bottom.
Fit each assembly into the wells of a standard 12-well plate for easy handling.
Add 500 µL of PBS to the well assembly and incubate for 10 min at room temperature with gentle shaking.
Remove PBS from the well assembly.
Repeat washing twice more with PBS for a total of three washes.
After the final PBS wash, add 500 µL of knockout-DMEM media to gels and incubate overnight at 37 °C.
Keep gels in 37 °C with media for up to 5 days before seeding cells.
The day before seeding cells, replace knockout-DMEM with complete KSR media.
Incubate the media change at 37 °C overnight.
Generate conditioned KSR media by culturing irradiated mouse embryonic fibroblasts in KSR media supplemented with 4 ng/mL basic fibroblast growth factor (bFGF).
Collect and replace media every 24 hours.
Aspirate the media from hESCs.
Briefly wash with knockout-DMEM media.
Add 0.05% trypsin-EDTA supplemented with 10 µM Y27632 to the dish and incubate at 37 °C for 5-10 minutes.
Add media with serum to inhibit trypsin.
Gently aspirate media and pipette over the dish to remove cells.
Continue pipetting gently to remove all cells and dissociate cell clusters into single cells.
Collect the cell suspension and centrifuge at 200 x g for 3 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in an equivalent volume of KSR media to wash.
Centrifuge at 200 x g for 3 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in conditioned KSR media supplemented with 10 ng/mL bFGF and 10 µM Y27632.
Count the cells with a hemocytometer.
Adjust the cell suspension to a concentration of 300,000 cells per mL.
Pipette 500 µL of the cell suspension onto each patterned gel (150,000 cells per gel).
Three hours after seeding, use a pipette to carefully aspirate the media from each gel and replace with fresh conditioned KSR media supplemented with 10 ng/mL bFGF and 10 µM Y27632.
This removes excess cells that did not adhere to patterned regions of the polyacrylamide.
Carefully aspirate the media 24 hours after seeding using a pipette.
Exchange for conditioned KSR media supplemented with 10 ng/mL bFGF and 5 µM Y27632.
Aspirate the media 48 hours after seeding using a pipette.
Exchange for conditioned KSR media supplemented with 10 ng/mL bFGF.
